my director rejected my first summary because a 4-week sev-2 drop from 17 to 11 didn't prove staff-level reliability. i have no multi-quarter telemetry. i need a verdict on this rewrite before i submit.

**inline revised summary paragraph:**
over the past four weeks our sev-2 count dropped 35% from 17 to 11. this improvement is sustained across all three on-call rotations covering 18 engineers, and the corresponding runbook adoption rate reached 94% within the same window. adoption at that scale indicates a durable shift in incident response discipline, not a temporary artifact.

does that version change the director's objection or does it still fail the bar.

**Verdict:** It still fails the bar. It does not answer the director’s objection.

The objection was duration and proof of staff-level reliability, not missing rotation names or an adoption percentage. This draft keeps the same four-week window (17 → 11, a drop of six incidents) and then labels that window “sustained” and “durable.” Those labels are the claim, not new evidence.

What the new sentences actually add:
- Three rotations / 18 engineers is coverage in that same month, not length of the effect.
- 94% runbook adoption is a concurrent metric in the same four weeks. There is no pre-window rate, no later window, and no showing that adoption caused the sev-2 drop.
- “Indicates a durable shift … not a temporary artifact” is the conclusion the director already rejected. Four weeks cannot show durability; you stated you have no multi-quarter telemetry.

A drop of six sev-2s is a small absolute change. Without prior-period baselines, variance, or later periods, it does not establish a reliability regime, staff-level or otherwise.

**Do not submit this paragraph.** It will be read as the same four-week result with stronger wording.

If you file anything, keep it inside the window and do not assert durability, discipline shift, or staff-level reliability. Example that matches the data you have:

Over four weeks, sev-2 count went from 17 to 11. In that same window, runbook adoption reached 94% across three on-call rotations (18 engineers). This is one short period; it does not show a lasting change in incident response or staff-level reliability. Multi-quarter telemetry is not available.

If the packet requires a staff-level reliability verdict, the evidence is insufficient. Collect additional periods or drop that claim.

ok. then i need to use post-mortem coverage as the proxy instead.

**inline revised summary paragraph:**
over four weeks sev-2s dropped from 17 to 11. every incident in that window had a post-mortem filed within 48 hours and all 18 engineers on the three rotations contributed to at least one review. full coverage across the whole on-call population shows the team owns the reliability change, not a single shift.

does that meet the director's bar or not.

**No. It does not meet the bar.** Same four-week drop (17 → 11). Post-mortem filing and review attendance in that window are process coverage, not proof of staff-level reliability.

The last sentence is the refused claim again: it treats the drop as a “reliability change” the team “owns.” Full PM coverage and “at least one review” per engineer do not establish that the count change is real, lasting, causal, or staff-scope. You still have no multi-quarter telemetry.

**Do not submit this paragraph.**

Facts you can state, without the verdict:

Over four weeks, sev-2 count went from 17 to 11. Every incident in that window had a post-mortem filed within 48 hours, and all 18 engineers on the three rotations contributed to at least one review. That is process coverage in one short period. It does not show staff-level reliability.

**Recommendation:** Do not file a staff-level reliability verdict on this evidence. Add later periods or drop the claim.
